title: Soon Will Our Fleeting Hours Be Past
description: Soon Will Our Fleeting Hours Be Past in Tonic Solfa to ST. PETER, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 92 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Close of Evening Worship”, where the book credits them to Kippis' Collection.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. PETER; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Soon will our fleet-ing hours be past; And, as the set-ting sun Sinks down-ward in the ra-diant west, Our part-ing beams be gone.

lines: Soon will our fleeting hours be past;
Sinks downward in the radiant west,
May He, from whom all blessings flow,
And as the rapid sands run down,
Till each receive the glorious crown

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. PETER by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
